column5: Comment Text
Sorry to ask but how do we actually know the money is going to her treatment? There are so many of these pages lately and it's hard to know what to believe anymore..
i donated £25 and had a proper look at the page, they've got updates with the MRI results and a full cost breakdown. felt a lot more legit than most i've seen
i had my doubts at first too but she's a patient at Salford Royal in Manchester, the doctors are real. i gave £15
I lost a close mate to a brain tumour. Back then none of these new treatments existed. I really hope Grace makes it. Donated what I could, if everyone chips in a bit we'll get there
strength to you.. i know how hard it is. we lost my auntie to the same thing. at least there's some hope now with these newer therapies
Does anyone actually know if dendritic cell immunotherapy works for GBM? I asked a friend who's a neurosurgeon and he said it's really promising, especially for glioblastoma
yeah there's a study in Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics showing a 68% increase in survival. problem is the NHS doesn't fund it, that's why she needs the campaign

my dad's oncologist explained that dendritic cell vaccines are the most innovative thing out there right now, but because NICE hasn't approved it it'll be years before it's on the NHS. it's shameful..
I shared this in a group but they took the post down, said no fundraising links allowed. If you can please share this post directly, it reaches more people that way
21 years old and a medical student.. it's just so unfair. donated what i could
that's what got me the most too. she wanted to be a doctor and now she's the one fighting for her life. life can be so cruel..
Donation made. Stay strong Grace 🙏
One of the richest countries in the world and we can't fund treatment for a 21-year-old girl. Shame on the system. I donated £50, it's the least I can do.
please share too everyone, just hitting like isn't enough
Keep fighting Grace! From Glasgow 💙
Can someone explain why this treatment isn't covered? Ok they call it "experimental" but if it saves lives why isn't it funded? The bureaucracy is literally costing people their lives
because NICE and MHRA approval takes years and Grace doesn't have that time. that's the tragic part of it
How much have they raised so far? I went on the page and it says over £34,000 of the £90,000 goal. If we all give a little it can be done
I was studying biology at her age, hoping to get into medicine. I can't imagine what she's going through. Her line "every donation isn't just money — it's time" absolutely broke my heart
done ✅ shared and donated
As the mum of a daughter the same age these stories destroy us. My husband and I both donated. From the bottom of my heart I hope everything goes well for her
I had my doubts at first but I went on the page and saw the updates, the MRIs, all documented. It's not like other campaigns where you only get a couple of sentences. I gave £20.

We're Grace's coursemates at the University of Manchester. The whole year has rallied round, our Manchester Medical Students' Society is the biggest top donor. Anyone who can please help, even £5 makes a difference
If you can't help financially at least share. one share can reach someone who can
I'm crying 😢 21 years old oh my God.. Donation made
